newsitem.title: JAPAN: Call rate up as mkt prefers short-term funds--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Call rate up as mkt prefers short-term funds--BOJ.

text.p: Market participants' preference for short-term money in their fund-raising activity is the cause of Thursday morning's rise in Japan's overnight call rate, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said.
Unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.53 percent this morning, up from 0.51 percent on Wednesday.
While demand for funds was higher due to seasonal factors ahead of the fiscal year-end in March, market participants were concentrating their efforts on raising short-term funds, the official said.
"Market participants are in no hurry to raise long-term money, as they do not expect a near-term change in monetary policy," said the official.
Asked about the overnight rate's rising trend, the official said: "The BOJ has been providing liquidity needed to meet the market's requirement, and will continue to do so."
